title: TS SDK: streaming-friendly discriminated union + Zod/JSON-Schema helpers for typegen
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a production-ready flow in the TypeScript SDK codegen that emits discriminated unions with first-class runtime validators for both Zod and JSON-Schema consumption, with special streaming ergonomics so partial/streamed responses can be validated incrementally. Goal: reduce runtime surprises for structured outputs and make streaming parser + validation easy for client apps.
background: Current typegen emits TypeScript types and a naive runtime validator for simple shapes. Customers and internal SDK users report two pain points: 1) discriminated unions are fragile at runtime when discriminator names vary across model prompts, and 2) streaming responses that yield partial JSON or incremental shape fragments can't be validated easily with existing zod/.parse() flows. This ticket scopes a solution that ties codegen, runtime helpers, and streaming-friendly validators together.
out_of_scope: Python and Go SDKs (separate tickets), server-side enforcement of discriminator correctness, changing model schema contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Codegen emits a config-driven discriminator map and TypeScript types for unions
Zod helper factories generated alongside types that validate both full objects and incremental partials
JSON-Schema artifacts generated for each union variant and for the union itself
Runtime helpers expose: isUnionVariant(obj, variantName), streamValidate(chunkStream, options) and a safeParsePartial(buffer) API
End-to-end test that streams a 3-part JSON payload and validates as chunks arrive
Docs + example in SDK repo: how to declare discriminator field name and value mapping in prompter schema
No runtime size regression >5% in benchmark harness for common generation scenarios
design_decisions: Use a single canonical discriminator name in generated code, configurable via @discriminator('field') in model schema metadata
Generated runtime will prefer Zod when available, and fall back to a small runtime guard when zod is not installed at consumer runtime
Support an explicit mapping table for discriminator values to Variant name to handle synonyms (eg. 'message_type' -> 'text' | 'choice')

Streaming validation operates on a line-delimited / boundary-token protocol: the SDK will buffer until it detects a boundary token or a complete JSON value, validate incrementally, and expose partial typed values via an async iterator
Keep JSON-Schema generation narrowly typed (no $ref bundles) to keep artifacts simple for downstream validators
implementation_notes: Add new codegen flag --discriminator-field and --discriminator-map (JSON string) to tsdk-codegen CLI
Codegen output: types.ts, validators.zod.ts (optional), validators.runtime.ts (always emitted), schemas.json (json-schema per type)
validators.zod.ts should export Z.union([...]) for the union and helper typed factories: createVariantGuard(VariantName) and safeParsePartial(buffer) which uses zod.safeParse for complete objects
validators.runtime.ts is a zero-deps fallback with structural checks and a small trie-based discriminator resolver for fast resolution
Streaming helper streamValidate(stream, {onPartial, onComplete, maxBufferBytes}) returns AsyncIterable<{variant, parsed, raw}>
Add integration tests under packages/ts-sdk/test/typegen-streaming with Node 18 stream.Readable simulating chunk boundaries and corrupted chunk fragments
Benchmark the runtime guards in ci/perf against the existing naive validators using the 'generation-latency' harness
progress_updates: 2025-02-14 - Kickoff: scoped feature, agreed on default discriminator name 'type' but allowed to override via metadata. Assigned prototype to Ethan.
2025-02-17 - Prototype: generated validators.runtime.ts that can detect discriminator in a mixed-case mapping and perform O(1) variant resolution. Basic unit tests passing.

2025-02-19 - Found an edge case: models returning partial JSON arrays inside the variant payload break naive boundary detection. Decided to switch to a boundary-token approach (e.g., <EVENT_BOUNDARY>) for streaming model responses in examples and docs.
2025-02-22 - PR opened (WIP) with codegen changes and runtime fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1284

2025-02-24 - Design review with DX and PM: agreed to keep Zod artifact optional to avoid adding zod as direct dependency; updated docs to show how to opt into zod generation. PM requested example for canary rollout with mixed discriminator values.
2025-02-26 - Implemented streamValidate async iterator + tests for chunked JSON; failing case for nested arrays fixed by detecting balanced braces before parse attempt
test_plan: Unit: validator.runtime - exhaustive tests for discriminator mapping, missing fields, and extra fields
Unit: validator.zod - when zod artifact generated, zod.safeParse should produce same discriminated variant as runtime guard
Integration: streamValidate with 0..3 chunk boundaries, corrupted chunk inserted, ensure partials are emitted and final combine equals expected object
E2E: sample app in examples/streaming-forms that consumes the async iterator and renders variant-specific UI without waiting for full payload
Perf: run generation-latency harness and assert <=5% added overhead for validator.runtime on median path
open_questions: Should the SDK actively insert boundary tokens when calling hosted model endpoints, or only document and show examples?
Do we expose an opinionated 'discriminatorHint' in the runtime to allow fuzzy matching of discriminator values (levenshtein)?
If Zod is generated but consumer has incompatible zod version, should we ship a compatibility shim or error at import-time?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large streaming buffers leading to high memory use. Mitigation: expose maxBufferBytes and recommend application-level backpressure.
Risk: Consumers relying on ad-hoc discriminator names. Mitigation: provide migration guide and a small linter rule to check generator-config vs prompt schemas.
Risk: Zod version skew. Mitigation: keep Zod artifacts strictly optional and provide a build-time codegen mode that inlines lightweight zod-like validators for consumers who opt-in
follow_up_tasks: Create equivalent Go SDK primitives for streamValidate and runtime guards (separate ticket)
Add a console feature to display discriminator mismatch telemetry per route
Add example 'boundary token' option in hosted API docs and consider small server-side helper to emit tokens for streaming responses
notes_for_reviewers: Look specifically at validators.runtime.ts performance characteristics and the trie-based discriminator resolver
Check generated artifacts for clarity: avoid excessive duplication between validators.zod.ts and validators.runtime.ts
Confirm that streaming async iterator surface is ergonomic for typical React/Next apps (example included)
